lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Let's define the nodes of a cluster.
Your site has more than a controller and a worker? The nodes list picks the roles, the number of workers, and what each node gets.
There are four roles. Exactly one controller runs slurmctld, and one or more workers run slurmd.
A db node adds accounting, with MariaDB and slurmdbd. A submitter has the client commands, for submitting jobs. Both are optional.
When a node needs only a role and a count, the shorthand is enough: a bare role, or a role with a count.
It means the same as the full form, and both can be mixed in one list.
Workers are managed by default: sind starts slurmd and adds them to the Slurm configuration.
With managed set to false, a worker is just a container, to test how nodes register, or join later.
Nodes get no extra privileges by default. For FUSE file systems, for example, grant a capability and a device to the nodes that need them.
You can add workers later, too. Run sind create worker with the count and unmanaged flags for two unmanaged workers.
New workers copy the capabilities and devices of the newest worker, unless flags replace them.
So: one controller, one or more workers, and an optional db node and submitter. Shorthand for the simple cases, and privileges only where needed.
Next up: realms, to run clusters side by side. See you there!
